environment.procstatMethod: tests/perf/procstat (GetProcessMemoryInfo/GetProcessTimes on Windows); handles is null there
environment.dataRootDeltaNote: files created by the product during the run (startup scaffolding such as cookie-secret.txt, stats.json, _storage/ and .migrated markers, plus the chat this harness saves) and files removed; the harness itself only writes the saved chat and the card mtime
environment.leftoverCheck: tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq <binary basename>" after the final stop; empty means no orphan of this binary survived the run

parameters.port: every boot: a fresh free loopback port
parameters.calibrationRequest: one POST /api/characters/all before the soak clock, to learn the probe card's real name
parameters.concurrency: one request in flight; the loop never pipelines and resynchronises instead of bursting

restarts.stopModeNote: Windows has no SIGTERM delivery to a console process: taskkill /T is attempted first and /T /F only if the process survives. The exact mode per restart is in restarts[].stopMode, so a graceful-drain claim cannot be made from this artifact.

stop.mode: taskkill /T refused (exit 128: ERROR: The process with PID 13264 (child process of PID 9964) could not be terminated. Reason: This process can only be terminated forcefully (with /F option). ); forced with taskkill /T /F

rssTrend.reason: RSS is the only external memory observable; live heap and Go allocator retention are not separable from outside, so an upward RSS slope is not evidence of a leak

externalModification.method: fs.utimes on one card PNG (bytes untouched), then POST /api/characters/all; assert 200 and the card avatar/name still present

rssTrend.reason: RSS is the only external memory observable; live heap and Go allocator retention are not separable from outside, so an upward RSS slope is not evidence of a leak

memory.leakVerdictReason: RSS is the only external memory observable. Live heap and Go allocator retention are not separable from outside the process, so neither an upward slope nor a plateau proves or disproves a leak. A leak claim needs an in-process heap profile (not exposed by this binary).
memory.handlesReason: procstat reports handles=null on Windows (GetProcessHandleCount is not sampled); no handle/FD count is claimed anywhere in this artifact.

cpu.method: procstat GetProcessTimes deltas per segment (first vs last sample of that boot)

notes: handles/FDs are NOT measured: procstat reports handles=null on Windows and no GetProcessHandleCount sample exists, so this artifact claims no FD count.
goroutine count is NOT measured: it is not observable from outside the process and the product exposes no pprof endpoint; adding one would change the binary under test.

provider streaming/generation is NOT measured: the soak drives storage and settings routes only, issues no provider request and consumes no SSE stream. A provider soak needs a controlled peer plus credentials.

graceful shutdown is NOT measured: Windows cannot deliver SIGTERM to a console process, so the stop is taskkill /T (forced /T /F when refused); shutdown-flush behaviour is therefore not exercised by this artifact.
a LEAK is UNPROVEN: RSS is the only external memory observable, and live heap vs allocator retention cannot be separated from it.
same-port restart is NOT measured: every boot takes a fresh loopback port, so TCP state or a pooled connection to the previous origin cannot manufacture a restart failure.
the chat-save integrity check compares the last successfully saved array to the HTTP read-back AND to the on-disk bytes; a mismatch aborts the run rather than overwriting the evidence.
latencies are loopback and include harness-side body consumption; on a shared host they are not an SLO. The sample count is stated beside every percentile.
